title: Per-turn model and effort routing
description: Pick which model tier or thinking effort a coding task needs

tier.instructions: Which model tier should handle this next agent turn? Pick the cheapest tier that will still do it correctly.

criteria.haiku: Trivial or mechanical: rename, typo, formatting, listing, simple lookup, one-line edit
criteria.sonnet: Routine engineering: implement a well-specified feature, write tests, a bug fix with a known cause, small refactor
criteria.opus: Hard: subtle concurrency or security reasoning, architecture or migration design, unknown root cause across many components

deep.instructions: Does this task require deep multi-step reasoning, where a fast shallow answer would likely be wrong?

criteria.true: Requires careful multi-step reasoning, tradeoff analysis, or hunting a subtle bug
criteria.false: Mechanical, well-specified, or a lookup; no deep reasoning needed

cx.instructions: How complex is this task for a coding agent?
criteria: hard: subtle bugs or design decisions
expert: deep reasoning over many interacting components

combine: opus if cx >= cx_opus; opus if tier == 'opus'; opus if tier == 'sonnet' and tier.p < tier_min_p; sonnet if tier == 'haiku' and tier.p < tier_min_p; haiku if tier == 'haiku' and deep <= haiku_deep_max and tier.p >= haiku_p; sonnet otherwise

effort.combine: high if deep >= deep_high; high if cx >= cx_opus; low if tier == 'haiku' and deep <= haiku_deep_max; medium otherwise

limitations: routes on the summary only (a lazy summary routes cheap)
the sonnet middle band is soft (confidence 0.43 on a clean feature and on a flaky test)
the 5-way effort choice is a secondary signal only
kill switch OPENJEV_MCP_ROUTING=off returns sonnet without a read
notes: # deviation: spec 2.18/5.8: decisions are ordered sonnet, haiku, opus so a fail-open override gives the safe default sonnet; tiers is not an input (the verbatim tier criteria are fixed); effort is always returned in outputs; a degraded run returns sonnet without the effort medium
